newsitem.title: INDIA: Oil producers, consumers begin gathering at Goa meet.
newsitem.headline: Oil producers, consumers begin gathering at Goa meet.

text.p: Representatives of the world's leading oil producers and consumers began arriving for talks in the Indian resort of Goa on Thursday against a background of the highest oil prices in almost six years.

Indian officials said the discussions, starting on Saturday, would focus on the growing energy needs of emerging economies, struggling to handle rising oil import bills while sustaining economic growth.
North Sea Brent crude is now trading around US$24 per barrel, the highest levels since the Gulf War.
Officials from 37 countries were scheduled to arrive over the next two days, including 16 at the ministerial level.

Oil producers will be strongly represented, but a poor response from consumers, repeating the pattern of previous years, indicates that most major oil users believe there is little concrete to be gained from the discussions, initiated in the wake of the 1990-1991 Gulf War.
The fifth in a series of international conferences will be opened on Friday by Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda.
"The talks will cover global energy cooperation issues between producer and consumer countries," said Bikash Bora, chairman of the state-run Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Ltd (ONGC).
"Security of consumers will be one issue which will be discussed, if not in the conference, in bilateral meetings," Bora said.
Conference officials said security of supply and demand and technological partnerships between producers and consumers would be discussed.

Saudi Oil Minister Ali al-Nuaimi will not attend the energy talks but Iranian Oil Minister Gholamreza Aghazadeh was expected arrive at the beach resort, 60 kms from Goa's capital Panaji, on Thursday, conference officials said.
Saudi Arabia, the world's biggest oil producer and exporter, will be represented by Ministry Director Prince Abdul Aziz bin Salman.
OPEC ministers from Indonesia, Nigeria, Qatar, the United Arab Emirates and Venezuela are expected to attend.

Russian Fuels and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov, Norway's new energy minister, Grete Faremo, Egyptian Petroleum Minister Hamdi El Banbi and Mexico's Oil Minister Jorge Naverrete will represent major non-OPEC oil production.
Other OPEC members, including Kuwait and Iraq, are sending oil ministry officials.
Ministerial representation for consumer countries is restricted to India, Portugal and South Africa. Major consumers the United States, Germany, Japan and France are sending ministry officials.
The previous ministerial level conferences in the series were held in Paris, Solstand in Norway, Cartagena in Spain, and in Venezuela.
Norway and Brazil, one a major producer and the other a major consuming country, are the co-sponsors for the Goa meeting.
Conference officials said the meeting would also cover global energy policy inter-relationships.
Bora said the international price of crude oil was unlikely to come up at the talks.
